title: Hierarchical Text-Conditional Image Generation with CLIP Latents
layout_note: A dotted diagonal line splits the figure into the CLIP training process above and the text-to-image generation process below; the text encoder on the left straddles both and its embedding is bracketed into both halves.
grouping: No frames for the halves; a single dotted rule (stepping diagonally around the text encoder) separates them; in the lower half the two prior variants are grey rounded boxes stacked one above the other under the label 'prior'.
shapes_depth: Encoders as large flat trapezoids (text encoder blue, image encoder brown); embeddings as vertical columns of shaded square cells; the prior variants drawn as small token-circle diagrams inside grey rounded boxes; the decoder as three columns of coloured circles; no shadows.
proposed_highlight: The new parts (prior and decoder) sit in the lower half and are labelled in plain text beneath; the colour hand-off from blue text-embedding cells to brown image-embedding cells across the prior shows what the prior does.
lesson: Show a model built on a pretrained one by drawing the pretrained training above a dotted rule and the new generation pipeline below, sharing one input encoder that straddles the rule.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; widely known as DALL-E 2 (the paper calls the model unCLIP); no venue printed on the first page.

arrangement.units: two unframed horizontal lanes separated by a dotted rule: CLIP training (top) and prior + decoder generation (bottom)
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted text prompt in large blue type at the far left
arrangement.losses_at: the 'CLIP objective' as a double-headed arrow between the text and image embeddings in the top lane; no loss drawn for prior or decoder
arrangement.shared: one text encoder on the left whose output embedding is split by a bracket into both lanes

taxonomy.task: text-to-image generation via CLIP image embeddings
taxonomy.note: the prior is drawn in two variants (autoregressive, diffusion); diffusion decoder

core.what: one text encoder at the far left whose embedding is bracketed into two lanes split by a stepped dotted rule: the CLIP training lane above and the prior-plus-decoder generation lane below

relations.form: in the top lane the text-embedding column and the image-embedding column face each other across a double-headed 'CLIP objective' arrow, the image encoder trapezoid and the real corgi image behind it on the right
bottom lane runs left to right: text embedding -> prior box -> image-embedding column -> decoder (columns of circles) -> generated corgi image
the prior's two variants stacked as grey rounded boxes, an autoregressive one drawn as attention arcs over a row of circles above a diffusion one drawn as three columns of circles
two unframed horizontal lanes (training above, generation below) separated by a dotted rule that steps down around the text encoder

channels.colour: modality: blue for text (prompt type, text encoder, text-embedding cells) and brown for image (image encoder, image-embedding cells); the decoder's circles shade blue -> purple -> brown, so colour also tracks progress from text to image there
channels.shape: trapezoids are encoders, vertical cell columns are embeddings, grey rounded boxes are the prior variants, circle columns are diffusion steps
channels.line: solid arrows are data flow; the double-headed arrow is the contrastive objective; the dotted rule is the lane divider
channels.frame: none for the lanes; only the two prior variants are boxed

quality.strengths: The shared text encoder straddles the dotted rule so its reuse in both lanes is visible by position; embeddings are drawn as cell columns between encoders and the objective; the blue-to-brown cell colour across the prior shows what the prior produces; real prompt and generated images are drawn as data.
quality.weaknesses: The prior and decoder, the paper's contribution, are labelled only by small text under the bottom lane and are no larger than the pretrained CLIP part; the decoder's circle columns blend colour meanings (modality vs denoising progress); no objective is drawn for the prior or decoder.

insights.structure: Two lanes split by a stepped dotted rule, CLIP training above and generation below, with the text encoder trapezoid on the left spanning both and a bracket fanning its embedding into each lane.
insights.data: The input is a quoted prompt in large blue text, embeddings are vertical columns of shaded cells coloured by modality (blue text, brown image), and outputs are real generated corgi images at the right edge of each lane.
insights.emphasis: The prior's two variants are stacked grey boxes with miniature attention-arc and diffusion-circle diagrams, and the cell colour switching from blue to brown across them shows the text-to-image embedding mapping.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right in both lanes: prompt -> text encoder -> embedding -> (CLIP objective | prior -> decoder) -> image.
insights.avoid: The dotted divider bends diagonally under the text encoder and the two halves have no titles, so a reader must rely on the caption to know the top lane is training-only.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
